record.paper_title: 二分決定グラフに基づく計算複雑さに関する未解決問題について
record.original_question: Determine the relationship between SL and l-LogCut. Here SL is the class of languages accepted by logarithmic-space symmetric Turing machines, meaning nondeterministic Turing machines whose every transition has the corresponding reverse transition, and l-LogCut is the ordered-input version of the O(log n)-cutwidth polynomial-size circuit class. Is SL contained in l-LogCut, does l-LogCut contain SL, are the two equal, or are they incomparable?

evidence.quote: SL とは、対数領域の対称 Turing 機械で受理される言語のクラスである。
SL l-LogCut の間の関係もわかっていない。

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the complexity class SL (symmetric logspace) as the class of languages accepted by symmetric Turing machines using O(log n) work tape space, where a symmetric Turing machine is a nondeterministic Turing machine whose transition relation is symmetric: for every allowed transition between two configurations, the reverse transition is also allowed.

Define the complexity class l-LogCut as the ordered-input version of the class of languages decided by polynomial-size Boolean circuit families {C_n} of cutwidth O(log n). Here the cutwidth of a Boolean circuit (viewed as a directed acyclic graph with input gates, internal gates, and one output gate, drawn with all gates placed on a horizontal line in some order) is the maximum, over all vertical cuts of the line, of the number of wires crossing the cut; "ordered-input" means that for each n the input bits x_1, …, x_n appear at fixed positions in this left-to-right order at the leftmost end of the layout.

Determine the inclusion relationship between SL and l-LogCut: prove one of the following statements, or show that the question is independent of standard assumptions:
(a) SL ⊆ l-LogCut,
(b) l-LogCut ⊆ SL,
(c) SL = l-LogCut,
(d) SL and l-LogCut are incomparable under inclusion.
artifact.category_tag: Space-bounded complexity classes and bounded-cutwidth circuits
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not locate any published result settling the inclusion relationship between SL and the bounded-cutwidth circuit class l-LogCut. While Reingold's 2005 theorem established SL = L, no source found relates L (or SL) to the ordered-input O(log n)-cutwidth polynomial-size circuit class l-LogCut, so the status of the specific comparison remains unverified.

status_evidence.title: SL (complexity) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Reingold's result shows that when limited to log space, the symmetric Turing machine is equivalent in power to the deterministic Turing machine (SL = L).
status_evidence.claim: SL has been characterized (SL=L), but no statement is given relating SL to l-LogCut.

status_evidence.title: Circuit Complexity of Bounded Planar Cutwidth Graph Matching
status_evidence.snippet: Studies circuits and graphs with bounded cutwidth, related to small-space complexity classes.
status_evidence.claim: Bounded-cutwidth circuit classes are studied but no direct comparison with SL is reported.
